Scenario.Description: Check which Office applications are running and list open documents. Sets context for subsequent scenarios.

1. Call MSOfficeWin LISTDOCS to enumerate all open Word/Excel/PowerPoint documents. LISTDOCS returns an array with: name, path, appType (word/excel/powerpoint), saved (bool), sheets (Excel only), slides (PowerPoint only). If LISTDOCS returns RETRYLATER, Office is still initialising — wait 2 s and retry. 2. Call KeyWin LISTWINDOWS to discover window handles. Office windows have titles like: Word: "Document1 - Word" or "filename.docx - Word" Excel: "Book1 - Excel" or "filename.xlsx - Excel" PowerPoint: "Presentation1 - PowerPoint" Match by title substring to find HANDLE:<hwnd>. 3. If no Office process is running, use scenario id="newdoc-word" / "newdoc-excel" / "newdoc-powerpoint" to start one. 4. If a blocking dialog is detected (see scenario id="dismiss-office-dialog"), dismiss it before proceeding.
Open a blank Microsoft Word document.

1. Call MSOfficeWin NEWDOC target=word. ─ If Word is already running: adds a new document to the existing instance. ─ If Word is not running: starts WINWORD.EXE and creates Document1. ─ RETRYLATER means COM is busy (Office initialising) — wait 3 s and retry once.
2. After success, call MSOfficeWin LISTDOCS to verify the document appears. The new document is typically named "DocumentN" (where N is a counter, locale-dependent: "Dokument1" in Czech, "Document1" in English).
3. Call MSOfficeWin FOCUS target=word to bring the window to front (required for cooperative/showcase mode so the user can see the document).
4. Call KeyWin LISTWINDOWS to discover HANDLE:<hwnd> of the Word window. Look for a window whose title ends in "- Word" and is not a dialog.
5. (Optional) Call screenshotWindow targetId=HANDLE:<hwnd> to visually verify the document state before writing content.
KNOWN SIDE-EFFECTS: • First launch: Word may show an "Account / Sign-in" modal. Detect via KeyWin LISTWINDOWS (title "Sign in to set up Office" or "Activate Office"). Dismiss with: KeyWin SENDKEYS {ESC} or CLICKNAME "Close". • Protected View: if a previously recovered file opened in Protected View, a yellow bar shows "Enable Editing". For new blank documents this does not occur. • "Document Recovery" task pane: appears after a crash. Ignore for new docs unless it blocks — in that case use scenario id="dismiss-office-dialog".

Step.note: create blank Word document; starts WINWORD.EXE if not running

Scenario.Description: Open a blank Microsoft Excel workbook.

1. Call MSOfficeWin NEWDOC target=excel. ─ RETRYLATER: COM busy — wait 3 s and retry once. ─ On success, Excel adds a new workbook named "BookN" (locale-dependent: "Sešit1" in Czech, "Book1" in English).
2. Call MSOfficeWin LISTDOCS to confirm the workbook appears with appType="excel". Note: LISTDOCS for Excel also returns sheets[] — verify at least one sheet exists.
3. Call MSOfficeWin FOCUS target=excel.
4. Call KeyWin LISTWINDOWS → find window with title ending in "- Excel". Record HANDLE:<hwnd>.
KNOWN SIDE-EFFECTS: • Excel may show "Protected View" for files downloaded from the internet. For brand-new workbooks this should not occur. • COM sometimes triggers "Excel is waiting for another application to complete an OLE action" dialog. This blocks all COM calls. KeyWin LISTWINDOWS will show a window titled "Microsoft Excel" with short description. Dismiss with KeyWin SENDKEYS {ENTER} on HANDLE:<hwnd> of that dialog.

Step.note: create blank Excel workbook; starts EXCEL.EXE if not running

Scenario.Description: Open a blank Microsoft PowerPoint presentation.

1. Call MSOfficeWin NEWDOC target=powerpoint. ─ RETRYLATER: COM busy (PowerPoint initialising or busy with animation) — wait 3 s and retry up to 3 times. ─ PowerPoint has slower COM start-up than Word/Excel; first launch may take 5–10 s. ─ On success, a new presentation named "PresentationN" is created with 1 blank slide.
2. Call MSOfficeWin LISTDOCS to confirm appType="powerpoint" and slides[0] exists.
3. Call MSOfficeWin FOCUS target=powerpoint.
4. Call KeyWin LISTWINDOWS → find window with title ending in "- PowerPoint". Record HANDLE:<hwnd>.
KNOWN SIDE-EFFECTS: • PowerPoint may show a "New Presentation" / template chooser dialog on first run. If KeyWin LISTWINDOWS shows a window with class "#32770" (dialog) whose title does NOT contain "PowerPoint", that is the template chooser. Dismiss: KeyWin SENDKEYS {ESC} on HANDLE:<hwnd> of that dialog. • The presentation window title may briefly read "Presentation1" before a slide is loaded. Call LISTDOCS and verify slides count > 0 before interacting.

Step.note: create blank PowerPoint presentation; starts POWERPNT.EXE if not running

Scenario.Description: Capture a screenshot of the Office application window for visual verification.

Prerequisite: {{hwnd}} must be set (call KeyWin LISTWINDOWS first).
Use the MCP screenshotWindow tool with targetId=HANDLE:{{hwnd}}. The tool returns an inline PNG image so you can visually: • Verify the document content (text, cells, slides) • Detect dialog bars (Protected View, macro security, sign-in) • Confirm the correct window is active • Check for UI state after NEWDOC (blank doc vs template chooser)
Alternative — full screen: call screenshotWindow targetId="SYSTEM" (useful when hwnd is unknown or you want to see the entire desktop).
Use this screenshot step before and after significant document changes to provide visual evidence of the current state.

Step.note: capture window as base64 PNG; prefer the screenshotWindow MCP tool instead

Scenario.Description: Close an unexpected modal dialog that is blocking Office interaction.

Use this scenario when MSOfficeWin commands return RETRYLATER repeatedly and KeyWin LISTWINDOWS reveals a blocking dialog.
Identification — look for windows where: • process = WINWORD.EXE / EXCEL.EXE / POWERPNT.EXE • title does NOT match the normal document title pattern ("- Word", "- Excel", etc.) • OR title contains: "Sign in", "Activate", "Microsoft Office", "Security", "Protected", "Recover", "Update", "Compatibility", "Keep in Current Format"
Common dialogs and dismissal strategies: ┌─────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐ │ Dialog │ Dismissal │ ├─────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤ │ Sign in / Activate Office │ {ESC} or CLICKNAME "Close" │ │ Protected View (Enable Editing) │ {ALT+F} then {E} (Enable) │ │ Macro security blocked │ {ENTER} to close │ │ OLE busy ("waiting for app") │ {ENTER} │ │ Keep in Current Format? │ {ENTER} (keep) or {ALT+D} (discard) │ │ Unsaved changes on close │ {ALT+N} (don't save) or {ESC} │ │ Document Recovery task pane │ KeyWin CLICKNAME "Close" on pane │ └─────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘
After dismissal: 1. Call KeyWin LISTWINDOWS again to verify no more dialogs remain. 2. Retry the original MSOfficeWin command.

Step.note: ESC dismisses most cancellable Office dialogs

Scenario.Description:
Call MSOfficeWin SAVE target={{apptype}} (word / excel / powerpoint).
─ If the document has never been saved (name is "DocumentN" / "BookN" / etc.): SAVE triggers a "Save As" dialog (\#32770 class, title "Save As"). Use scenario id="save-as-dialog" to handle it. ─ If the document was previously saved, SAVE overwrites silently. ─ For Excel: if workbook contains macros (xlsm) and you save as xlsx, a compatibility dialog appears. Dismiss: KeyWin SENDKEYS {ENTER} (keep without macros) or {ESC} (cancel save).
After SAVE, verify via LISTDOCS that saved=true on the document entry.

When a "Save As" dialog appears (Win32 #32770, title "Save As"): 1. KeyWin LISTWINDOWS → find \#32770 dialog with title containing "Save" → record HANDLE:{{hwnd}}. 2. Type the target file path: KeyWin SENDKEYS "{{filepath}}" on HANDLE:{{hwnd}}. Clear any existing text first: KeyWin SENDKEYS {CTRL+A} then type path. 3. Confirm: KeyWin SENDKEYS {ENTER} on HANDLE:{{hwnd}}. The dialog closes and the document is saved at {{filepath}}. After closing, call LISTDOCS to verify saved=true and the path matches.

Step.note: select all text in filename box

Scenario.Description: To close an Office document: 1. Prefer saving first (scenario id="save-document") to avoid the "Save changes?" dialog. 2. Send {ALT+F4} via KeyWin to the target window HANDLE:{{hwnd}}. 3. If a "Save changes?" dialog appears: ─ {ALT+N} = Don't Save (discard changes, close immediately) ─ {ENTER} = Save (save, then close) ─ {ESC} = Cancel (abort close) 4. Verify via KeyWin LISTWINDOWS that the window is gone. 5. If this was the last document, Office may remain open (Application stays alive in COM). Call MSOfficeWin LISTDOCS to verify — if empty, Office is idle.

Step.note: send close request to Office window
